purpose: Create a chronological, append-only event history for each property investigation so the system can reconstruct what happened, which evidence and legal sources were used, what changed, what blocked progress, and why a publication state was reached.
event_principle: ONE MATERIAL STATE CHANGE → ONE TRACEABLE EVENT
append_only_rules: A correction creates a new event referencing the event being corrected.
A later event may supersede an earlier state but must not erase the historical event.
Publication and withdrawal events remain part of the permanent run history.
reconstruction_rules: A run must be reconstructable from its ordered events.
The latest valid event for a state dimension determines the current run state.
Conflicting events remain visible until a resolution event records the basis for resolution.
Source, document, legal and evidence references must remain linked to the event that used them.
A final answer must be traceable backward through its snapshot, quality gate, case file and material evidence/legal events.
hard_stops: Never overwrite or delete a material investigation event.
Never record a conclusion without identifying the engine or actor that produced it.
Never detach a material answer component from its supporting event chain.
Never treat event chronology as proof of the underlying property fact.
Never conceal failed retrievals, conflicts, blocked states or withdrawn answers.
